name: GreenStock
pitch: A live Laravel inventory pipeline for a plant nursery, built from scratch.
description: A from-scratch demo of a nursery/garden-supply inventory system, showing a Laravel ETL pipeline, database schema design, and a Vue 3 + Inertia front end, end to end — deployed as a real, publicly reachable demo rather than a localhost-only project.

highlights.title: Inventory as a ledger, not a counter
highlights.body: Stock isn't a mutable column on products — it's derived by summing an append-only inventory_movements table (in / out / adjustment). The number can never drift out of sync with the history that produced it, and that history is a useful audit trail on its own.

highlights.title: A real pipeline, not just a script
highlights.body: A supplier CSV feed runs through five single-purpose stages composed with Laravel's Illuminate\Pipeline\Pipeline: ValidateRow → NormalizeSku → UpsertProduct → RecordMovement → FlagLowStock. Each stage is independently testable and does exactly one job.

highlights.title: Restricted admin controls
highlights.body: A single admin-flagged account can issue manual stock adjustments with a required reason. Every adjustment lands on the same movement ledger as automated imports, so manual corrections stay part of the audit trail instead of bypassing it.

highlights.title: Actually deployed, not just runnable
highlights.body: Docker multi-stage build (Composer → Vite asset build → PHP runtime), running on Render's free tier against a separate managed Postgres database (Neon) so data survives container restarts. Chosen deliberately over a localhost-only demo — it forced real decisions about trusted proxies, env config, and cold starts.
